Title: 1943: The Battle of Midway
Description: Small handheld device/game with up, down, left, right navigational control. The device contains a button to turn sound on or off. The Acclaim handheld is loosely based off the Capcom arcade game of the same name. The game involved the player controlling an aircraft and winning multiple dogfights against other planes.

Title: 3-D Escape! 1000 Mazes
Description: 3-D Escape! 1000 Mazes is a tabletop puzzle game developed by Entex. Gameplay is in the first person, with a maze mode and adventure mode. Maze mode involved the player escaping from 1/1000 mazes, and adventure was the same, but required the collection of 3 artifacts to win first. The console is black, and has 4 arrow buttons to control movement.

Title: Advance Wars
Description: Advance Wars is a turn-based strategy game for the Nintendo Gameboy Advance developed by Intelligent Systems. Players would control their army with the goal of defeating another enemy army by capturing their headquarters or destroying their units on the map (known as routing them). Advance Wars has a campaign mode, tutorial section, and an arcade mode for setting high scores. After beating an enemy, the game would score the player on speed, power, and technique.
Articles: https://www.ign.com/games/advance-wars (IGN: Advance Wars)

Title: Advance Wars 2: Black Hole Rising
Description: Advance Wars 2: Black Hole Rising is a sequel to Advance War for the Nintendo Gameboy Advance. A new campaign mode is the driving force behind the sequel, and gameplay is the same requiring players to defeat all enemies and complete special objectives. The modes from the first game are unchanged and present in the sequel (War Room and versus). Players can fight each other using a Game Boy advance Link Cable.
Articles: https://www.ign.com/games/advance-wars-2-black-hole-rising (IGN:  Advance Wars 2: Black Hole Rising)

Title: Alien Revolt
Description: Hybrid reality game, which requires access to a GPRS network and a cell phone. Alien Revolt tells the story of a group of alien creatures who try to take over the Earth. Players can decide to join the human forces or the alien army, and choose between three classes of characters: Magus, Hacker, or Warrior, each of which has different attributes and abilities. Gameplay involves dueling opponents (who are within the 3km of proximity); however, the closer the opponent, the more likely that "shots fired" will be accurate. The purpose of gameplay is to kill opponents to gain points and to steal their possessions.

Title: Amazon
Description: A mobile handheld in the LCD Solar Power series by Bandai. This game flips open from a clamshell and features a small joystick. The player must jump travel throughout the Amazon while avoiding spiders, skeletons, crocodiles, and other threats to find treasure and earn points. Amazon (also known as Amazone) was on the double panel version of the LCD Solar Power.
Articles: https://www.handheldmuseum.com/Bandai/HikyoAmazon.htm (Handheld Museum: Bandai Hikyo Amazon or Amazone)

Title: Amidar
Description: Amidar is a table top electronic game developed by Gakken. Amidar has similar features and gameplay resembling Pac-Man, with enemies that kill upon contact and a similar game board. Players control a painter avoiding pigs on even numbered levels and an ape avoiding headhunters on odd numbered levels. The console is gray and white, with a red action button, and a white joystick for control. Amidar is also an arcade game and is featured for various consoles.

Title: Aquaplay
Description: Aquaplay is a toy produced by Brinquedos Estrela SA that was popular all over the world during the 1980s. It consists of a small container, made of transparent plastic, filled with water and sealed. A button (or two, depending on the model) on the base activated a mechanism in order to do the task of the game.

Title: Asphalt Urban GT
Description: Asphalt Urban GT is a racing video game that features high octane street racing. Players can choose from nine sports cars and race in eight different cities. To take the top spot, players will have to  speed up by skimming by other cars or drifting around tight corners. Police will try to stop you as you race. The game was also released on the Nintendo DS as one of its launch titles. It was also released on the Nokia N-Gage.

Title: Atari Lynx
Description: 16-bit handheld game console that was released by Atari Corporation in September 1989 in North America, and in Europe and Japan in 1990. It was the world's first handheld electronic game with a color LCD. It has a right and left handed configuration and the ability to zoom and alter in game sprites (Sprites are two-dimensional images or animations overlaid into a scene). Multiplayer was a main draw of the system's capabilities, allowing for up to 18 players using the Comlynx cord. A more compact version released as well.

Title: Backgammon
Description: Handheld game/console which allows gameplay of the traditional board game, Backgammon. This handheld has an LCD display. The game is single-player, requiring the player to play against the built in computer.
Articles: http://electro-gammon.net/gakken-backgammon/ (Electro-Gammon: Gakken Backgammon)

Title: Balloon Kid
Description: Balloon Kid is a flying platforming game for the Nintendo Game Boy. The goal of the game is for players to control Alice (the Balloon Kid) as she floats through a side scrolling level as she collects balloons and avoids obstacles, and in the end land safely with as many balloons as possible. A two player mode is available where two players race to see who can collect the most balloons. Alice can drop her balloons and walk if needed, in order to avoid obstacles.

Title: Banana Boat
Description: Banana Boat is a handheld game console developed by Takara. Players use the two action buttons to control their character. The system has a clock built in and the ability to link up to four consoles together to play multiplayer, using a cable that comes in box.

Title: Bandai Escape from the Devil's Doom
Description: Solar powered handheld console produced by Bandai for their LCD Solar Power series. In this game the player must dodge obstacles to earn points and eventually reach Heaven. The handheld alo goes by Tengoku & Jigoku, which is a Japanese translation  "heaven or hell."
Articles: http://handheldempire.com/game.jsp?game=347 (Handheld Empire: Escape from the Devil's Doom)

Title: Bandai Invader of the Mummy's Tomb LCD Solarpower
Description: Invader of the Mummy's Tomb is the smallest handheld game created by Bandai for their LCD Solarpower handheld.  Gameplay involves controlling an explorer in a pyramid to destroy snakes, scorpions, spiders, and mummy's for points. If the player defeats enough enemies, they can reach the hidden treasure in the pyramid to earn even more points. Bandai possibly created this game to capitalize on the popularity of Indiana Jones and the Raiders of the Lost Arc.
Articles: http://handheldempire.com/game.jsp?game=284 (Handheld Empire: Invaders of the Mummy's Tomb)

Title: Batman (Grandstand)
Description: This handheld game was released in 1989 and featured a game based off the Batman film that released the same year. This is an arcade style fighting game, where the player controls Batman and beats up enemies and avoids obstacles. The handheld had 7 buttons, 4 for movement, 1 for attacking, and 2 mode buttons. Two AAA batteries are required for powering the system, and there are 9 modes of difficulty in the game.
Articles: https://www.retrogames.co.uk/016496/Handheld/Batman-by-Grandstand (Retro Games UK)

Title: Bejeweled Multiplayer
Description: Bejeweled Multiplayer is an evolution of the classic game Bejeweled that allows the player to participate in one-on-one competitions and watch their friends compete in games. The objective of the game is to rotate different colors of gems in order to make them form horizontal or vertical lines of the same color. Once matched with gems of the same color, the sets will disappear and new gems will fall into their place. Various power-up gems can be obtained by creating large sequences of gems throughout the game, allowing the player to eliminate larger amounts of gems at a time.
Articles: https://www.verizon.com/about/news/jamdat-mobiles-bejeweled-multiplayer-now-available-verizon-wireless-get-it-now-customers (JAMDAT Mobile's Bejeweled Multiplayer Now Available to Verizon Wireless Get It Now Customers), https://www.gamespot.com/reviews/bejeweled-multiplayer-review/1900-6094028/ (Bejeweled Multiplayer Review), https://bejeweled.fandom.com/wiki/Bejeweled_Multiplayer (Bejeweled Multiplayer)

Title: Big Urban Game
Description: Big Urban Game (B.U.G.) consisted of a 5-day event occurring across the streets of Minneapolis and St. Paul in 2003 (Lantz, 2006); 200 square miles became a gameboard, transforming everyday spaces into a place for play. Three teams raced large, 25-foot-tall red, yellow, and blue inflatable game pieces through the cities orchestrated by public decisions registered on the B.U.G. Web site. The aim of B.U.G. is for teams to visit all the sites in the quickest time. It is up to the players to decide how they will move from site to site and, therefore, achieve the game’s goal.

Title: Black Knight Pinball
Description: Black Knight Pinball is an electronic handheld pinball game, based off the arcade game of the same name, developed by Entex. The handheld has 4 different skill levels and realistic pinball flappers that tilt if they are pressed too fast. The device is black with red flipper buttons, and a yellow shoot button. A portrait of a knight on a horse is underneath the lights needed to play.

Title: Black-Jack 21
Description: Early electronic blackjack game. Radio Shack created similar devices, such as blackjack calculators, as well.
Articles: https://americanhistory.si.edu/collections/search/object/nmah_334462 (Smithsonian Blackjack Calculator), https://www.pcmag.com/news/7-awesome-portable-electronic-games-of-the-1990s (7 Awesome Portable Electronic Games of the 1990s)

Title: BlackBerry 5810
Description: Monochrome mobile phone, runs Java platform, and 2G capable. One of the first smartphones it was mainly reserved for business due to its high $500 price point. The phone lacked a built-in microphone and speaker, but it came with a headset.
Articles: http://www.blackberry.com/news/connection/200201.shtml (The New BlackBerry 5810 Wireless Handheld), https://biztechmagazine.com/article/2016/11/blackberry-5810-kickstarted-mobile-work-era (BlackBerry 5810 Kickstarted the Mobile Work Era), https://uk.pcmag.com/first-looks/30688/blackberry-5810 (PC Magazine: BlackBerry 5810 Review)

Title: Blast It
Description: Blast It is a handheld electronic game developed by Entex. Gameplay is identical to other breakout games, in which a player would move a platform and bounce a ball to break objects above them. The console is white with 3 red directional buttons. All lights on the console are red and score is kept by 1s.

Title: Botfighters
URL: No website for game currently exists
Description: Botfighters is considered the first location-based mobile game. It was designed as an urban, massively multiplayer online role-playing game (MMORGP) which "uses GSM Network Cell identification" to find nearby players. The objective of the game was to locate, in the city, other player-robots and to engage in a battle to destroy them by "shooting" them. A successful shot gave depended on the players' distance to one another and the characters' strength. Players gain points by battling, and points allows players to purchase defensive protections, such as armors and shields. The game is "always-on," which means that a player can be attacked at any time and in any place where other players convene. Attack and counter-attacks were carried out by SMS commands initially, but later the game upgraded to a Java-based application.

Title: Brain Age: Train Your Brain in Minutes a Day!
Description: Brain Age is a mobile puzzle game developed by Nintendo for the Nintendo DS. Gameplay involves various puzzles, games, and questions focused on keeping certain parts of the brain active. Players would hold the DS on its side like a book and interact with games via the touch screen. Players could earn stamps and rewards for doing well on puzzles. Brain Age features voice control, age and date monitoring for puzzles, and was intended to be played everyday. Brain Age was the 4th best selling game on the Nintendo DS with 19.01 million units sold according to Nintendo.

Title: Breakout for Two
Description: A cross between soccer, tennis, and the game Breakout, in this game the player must use their stamina to kick a ball and break a picture of another player. The picture is made up of blocks.

Title: Bubble Bobble (Game Gear)
Description: Bubble Bobble is a classic platform arcade game that was ported to the Sega Game Gear in 1994. Players must control two dragons/dinosaurs in order to beat enemies and advance through all 100 levels. At the end of the game players have to beat a boss and can get 1 of 2 endings depending on if there are 1 or 2 players. Bubble Bobble is one of the first games to feature multiple endings. Bubble Bobble is one of the most ported games in history, being featured on numerous consoles.

Title: Can You See Me Now?
Developers: Blast Theory, Mixed Reality Lab (University of Nottingham)
URL: https://www.blasttheory.co.uk/projects/can-you-see-me-now/ (Can you see me now? | Blast Theory)
Description: Multiplayer hybrid reality game, in which players (called "runners") navigate a city with the goal of catching a remote, online player. While online players explored a 3D model of Sheffield on a computer, runners moved in the physical city using a personal digital assistant (PDA) equipped with both Global Positioning System (GPS) and a walkie-talke. Runners could see the location of online players on the PDA map and coordinate with each other via the walkie-talkie. The aim of online players not to be caught or seen by runners. If an online player got caught by a 'runner' they were knocked out of the game. The game has been re-enacted in many cities throughout the world, since its original release in Sheffield.

Title: Castle's Adventure
Description: Castle's Adventure is an electronic handheld game made by the Chinese company Sunwing. The polarizing filter over the LCD screen can flip up from the device.
Articles: http://handheldempire.com/game.jsp?game=1477 (Handheld Empire), https://www.handheldmuseum.com/Sunwing/CastlesAdventure.htm (Handheld Museum)

Title: Castlevania II: Belmont's Revenge
Description: Castlevania II: Belmont's Revenge is the sequel to Castlevania: The Adventure for the Nintendo Game Boy. Players traverse through side-scrolling levels in order to save Christopher Belmont's kidnapped son from Count Dracula. Belmont has a whip, holy water, and throwable axes to be used against enemies and level bosses. Belmont's Revenge utilizes a passcode based saving system adn features four levels, each with a unique theme and traps. Players can complete the levels in any order.

Title: Castlevania Legends
Description: Castlevania Legends is the third Castlevania game released for the Nintendo Game Boy. Gameplay requires players to traverse through side-scrolling levels, while defeating enemies and collecting items. The plot revolves around Sonia Belmont's quest to defeat Count Dracula in Transylvania during the Middle-Ages. Legends is single-player, incorporates password based save states, and has two difficulties (regular or invincible.)

Title: Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance
Description: Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance is a side-scrolling platform game fore the Nintendo Game Boy Advance. The plot revolves around Juste Belmont and his quest to retrieve a kidnapped friend. Players traverse through castles filled with monsters and obstacles while using a whip and a variety of other weapons and spells in order to reach the end. Role-playing elements are present in Harmony of Dissonance, the player receives experience points for defeating mini-bosses and bosses, which allow for an increase in health and damage. Two additional game modes are available, a boss rush mode, where the player must defeat all bosses in order, and Maxim mode, where the player controls Maxim, a character with more mobility but less weapon accessibility.

Title: Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin
Description: Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin is a side-scrolling platformer for the Nintendo DS, and a continuation of Castlevania: Bloodlines for the Sega Genesis. Players can swap between and control Johnathan and Charlotte as they aim to defeat Dracula. The story takes place during World War II, introducing more modern technologies to the series. Players must strategically use both characters in order to defeat enemies, solve puzzles, and avoid/destroy obstacles. A co-op boss rush mode and shop is available through the Nintendo Wi-Fi connection.

Title: Castlevania: The Adventure
Description: Castlevania: The Adventure is the first Castlevania game released for the Nintendo Game Boy. Players traverse through side-scrolling levels as they control Christopher Belmont in his quest to defeat Count Dracula. Gameplay requires the player to upgrade their whip and collect hearts to restore health. Their are four stages in the game, each with a time limit and final boss. The player completes the game when they defeat Dracula.

Title: Catchbob!
Developers: At École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne
Description: This is an application that engages a group of three to participate in a collaborative treasure hunt over the campus of École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne. Players can communicate with each other by drawing pictures, adding words, or providing other types on information on their devices to find each other. The device displays a campus map and the drawings are sent to each player. The players have to find the objects on the map and collaborate with each other to surround the object with a triangle formed by their individual positions. The game is used as a platform to run field experiments to understand how collaborative processes are impacted by information about another team's whereabouts.

Description: A classic game of "Tag, you're it" through a ipaq pocket PC interface, in which players use GPS to navigate the city and search for other participating players. Upon finding an opposing player, a player can "tag" them-- in which case, they must find a friend to free them before they can find other players to tag.

Title: CityExplorer
Description:
In CityExplorer, players take photographs with geographic information attached to create a database of points of interest of a city and categorize them.  It is a location-based game with a purpose:  to create geospatial data that could be used for many other purposes including non-gaming applications.  With multiple people "playing" the game, data can be captured and a city can be recreated digitally.

The gameplay of CityExplorer is in the real world with players utilizing their mobile devices to capture images and geographic information with the devices' camera and GPS systems.  To win the game, the player has to set as many geographic markers in a city game area.  Each city game area is divided into sections and the player who holds the most markers in a section wins that specific section and is awarded credits at the end of the game.  Players must create markers using pre-defined categories such as a "church."  In order to set a market, the player must (1) take a photo of the location, (2) enter in the name of the location, (3) get as close to the location as possible in order to get an accurate GPS reading, and (4) select the location category.  A GPS coordinate is captured at steps 1 and 2.  Once the player sets enough markers, they export the photographs and data to a computer to upload to the CityExplorer website.

The purpose of gameplay is to "shoot" other players, who have accepted a game play challenge. The players use the GPS information to determine the location of other players; they use their accelerometer to tilt their phone and angle shots toward opponents. In addition to firing shots at other players, players can also virtually destroy the physical structures of the city.

Title: Day Of The Figurines
Developers: Blast Theory, Mixed Reality Lab (University of Nottingham)
Description: Day of the Figurines is a pervasive game for mobile phones that is designed to be slow and interwoven with the patterns of players’ daily lives over the course of twenty-four days (each day that passes represents one hour in the gameworld). It is a massively multiplayer game, set in a fictional town that is littered, dark, and underpinned with steady decay. To begin the game, players are invited to create their own figurine: to name it, answer questions about its past and to describe how it is represented to other players. To interact in the game, players can remotely send SMS to indicate what they want their figurine to do. Further, players receive SMS indicating their figurine's status as well as inviting the players to make decisions or complete tasks for the town. The purpose of the game is for players to collaborate to sustain the town's sense of community.

Title: GPS::Tron
Description: GPS::Tron is a multiplayer game for java-enabled mobile phones that is a variation of the arcade classic racing game. Tron players move in real space, and GPS is used to track and locate users. GPS::Tron utilizes a cell phone that is connected—via Bluetooth—to an external GPS receiver. This racing game sets two players side-by-side on a digital grid, each driving a different colored vehicle. The players begin driving forward, leaving in their path a digital trail of their vehicle’s color. This trail forms a wall that neither player can cross again, thus making the goal of the game to trap the other player within the digital walls created by the vehicles. Players can collect bonus materials that allow them to get shields and breakthrough a trail left by opponents.The vehicles, however, do not necessarily need to be physically next to each other for the game to work. One player can begin the game on the streets of Los Angeles while the opponent begins the game on the streets of Sydney. Their locations are mapped onto the digital  interface, allowing players from around the globe to compete with each other.

Description: Galaxian 2 is a mobile handheld game developed by Entex. This device is based off the Bally/Midway arcade game, and is named "Galaxian 2" because of its multiplayer capability. Controls were on both sides of the console, and the gameplay is vertical.

Title: Galaxy Twinvader
Description: Handheld device with multi-directional controller and 3 inputs -- gameplay similar to the game space invaders. The console has a fire button, a joystick for control, a sound on/must switch, a demo button, and a reset button. The display had blue as the ship and red as the enemies players must shoot.

Title: Garfield (Konami)
Description: Garfield is a handheld game developed by Konami featuring the titular character from the hit franchise of the same name. The handheld is orange with a D-pad and action button for gameplay mechanics and 4 system control buttons. The game depicts a classic recurring Garfield scene where he performs on a fence in the middle of the night to a less than enthusiastic crowd. Gameplay involves controlling Garfield while avoiding trash thrown at him and collecting lasagna.

Title: Gargoyle’s Quest
Description: Gargoyle’s Quest is an action platforming game for the Nintendo Game Boy developed by Capcom. Gameplay is split into a top-down view in towns and the overworld and a side-scrolling platforming view. Players control the gargoyle Firebrand, who climbs, jumps, and clings to walls in order to defeat King Breager, who threatens the Ghoul Realm. Firebrand has a power called the Red Blaze, which is destined to save the world, players must use this power as a projectile to attack enemies. The Red Blaze can be powered up throughout gameplay, and is necessary in order to complete the story.

Description: The Geo TicTac Toe is a mobile location-based game, LBG. The game is to combine a player's intellectual and sportive skills. There are various tasks the player must do and find by using the TicTac toe board on their screen.

Title: Geocaching
Description: Geocaching is an outdoor activity, which involves players finding clues and GPS coordinates online and, then, seeking out a "cache" based on the clues and coordinates. The object of Geocaching is to decode the clues and coordinates to find the cache. Upon finding the cache, players typically sign their name to a log and, in some cases, leave objects behind (known as treasures or swag) which can be traded with other players who find the cache. Additionally, some caches contain "trackables," which are objects that contain unique identifiers. Players can collect trackables and move them to another cache in a different location; players who find trackables use the unique identifier to update their location, so that others can track their movement over time.

Title: Geodashing
URL: http://geodashing.gpsgames.org/ (Geodashing - Getting There is All the Fun)
Description: Geodashing involves players, across the world, racing to see who can visit the most number of dash points before a specific deadline. Dash points are specific locations that are randomly selected by computer algorithm and can be located anywhere. The objective of the game is for players to gain points for each place visited. Although there is no "winner," competition exists by seeing who can accumulate the most points. Unlike a similar game, Geocaching, there is no logbook, cache, or swag at a particular location. Players can play individual or in teams of people up to five.

Title: Gizmondo
Description: The Gizmondo is a handheld game console released by Tiger Telematics in 2005. The handheld could play games via cartridges, as well as other media. Gizmondo models are small with an LCD screen, featured four control buttons on the right, and a control dial on the left side of the console. This console is considered to be a massive failure due to the lack of advertising, low count of games (14), and the executive of Tiger Telematics being involved in the Swedish mafia.

After the game, teams get together at a pub and watch the photos and videos on a big screen. They vote via mobile phone on which team's photos they prefer the most.

Gameplay involves exploring, speaking to non-playable characters (NPCs), collecting upgrades, solving puzzles, and battling foes. Golden Sun was intentionally set to be  Nintendo 64 game, but due to development issues was pushed to the Game Boy Advance.

Title: Golden Sun: The Lost Age
Description: Golden Sun: The Lost Age is the sequel to Golden Sun for the Game Boy Advance. This game continues the story of the first game, and keeps all major gameplay features. Players can transfer their data (with a Game Boy Link cable)  from the first game and continue with their same stats and items. Completing both games with the same save will give the player additional awards. Golden Sun: The Lost Age allows players to complete objectives in their own order.

Description: Hamburger is a handheld console developed by Takara. Players use the 2 action buttons to control their character as they do simple tasks to earn score. The system has a built-in clock and can allow up to 4 consoles to be connected for multiplayer using a cable.

Title: Hockey
Description: Hockey is an electronic simulation game developed by Entex. Players could play against one another or a computer. Four yellow arrow keys determined player movement and a yellow shoot button was next to it. Players would look at lights on a hockey rink to determine where their player was and when to shoot if close enough while avoiding opposing players. The console is a dark green and features two sets of controls at opposite ends.

Description: A game of a PacMan played in the streets of Tokyo. Players are on one of two teams, either the PacMan team or the Ghost team. The PacMan team has two players that serve as PacMan, plus two helpers who are located remotely. The Ghost team has two ghosts, plus two helpers who are also located remotely. Title: Hyper Ski
Description: Handheld game focused on a skier avoiding obstacles, requires the user to tilt the device in order to make the "skier" move in the right direction (uses a steel ball to determine which direction the device is tilted). One of the potential photos that they can open offers the location of a hidden object. Once the hidden object is uncovered, the online player must ask a player in the physical world to navigate to that hidden object. Once a player in the physical world agrees to go find the hidden object, the physical world player begins receiving messages about a character "Frank" and his journey with the game's creator, which mirrors the journey that the physical world player is currently taking. Upon finding the hidden object (a postcard with a question), the physical world player then directs the question that is on the postcard to the online player.

Each insect in the game world is generated using the Bluetooth devices available in the player's vicinity. Title: Kangoku Lock
Description: Kangoku Lock is a handheld console developed by Takara. Players use the two action buttons to control their character as they do simple tasks to earn a score. The system has a built-in clock and can allow up to four consoles to be connected for multiplayer, using a cable that comes in-box.

Title: Karate King
Description: Small handheld device/game, allowing navigational control and two unique input controls (punch, kick/accelerate, break). The handheld took two AA batteries, and were marketed as being cheaper than the Nintendo Game Boy. Karate King allowed for one to two players, but not simultaneously. Gameplay involved kicking and punching your opponent to knock them out of 30 hit points.

Title: Keith Courage in Alpha Zones
Description: A sci-fi platformer for the TurboGrafx-16 and Turbo Express Handheld. Players control Keith Courage as he fights off an alien invasion with his sword. Keith Courage in Alpha Zones has seven levels, taking place in the vertically platforming overworld and the horizontal and vertically platforming underworld. Players must combat enemies in each setting, with the underworld being more difficult. This game is based on the anime Spirit Hero Wataru.

Title: Kirby & the Amazing Mirror
Description: Kirby & the Amazing Mirror is a platformer on the Gameboy Advance in the popular "Kirby" series of games. Players must explore levels while defeating enemies, solving puzzles, and collecting items. Kirby has the ability to copy enemies' abilities and use them for himself, helping the player traverse the game with different powers. The game takes place in a maze-like setting, in which the player can pick and choose where they want to go depending on the current power Kirby has. The player must collect 8 mirror fragments throughout the world in order to save Meta Knight and the Mirror World from an evil copy of Meta Knight, "Dark Meta Knight." Kirby & the Amazing Mirror is considered one of the best Kirby games.

Title: Kirby Super Star Ultra
Description: Kirby Super Star Ultra is a platforming anthology game for the Nintendo DS. It is an enhanced remake of Kirby Super Star (a game for the Super Nintendo). There are 11 different game modes, including seven from the original game and four new ones, which are modified versions of original modes. Six game modes are story driven, one is a racing game, three are for boss fight rematches, and one is an adventure/collection mode. Gameplay involves players controlling Kirby, who can fly and absorb the powers of enemies he absorb, while defeating enemies, avoiding obstacles, and solving puzzles. Multiplayer is possible through the DS's infrared connection and DS Download Play app. Additional players act as an assistant to Kirby, with his movement and strength, except the ability to change their power.

Title: Kirby's Dream Land
Description: Kirby's Dream Land is an action platformer for the Nintendo Game Boy. Players control Kirby as he jumps, runs, and flies through 2D levels in his quest to stop King Dedede from stealing all the food in Dream Land. The main method of attacking enemies is for the player to make Kirby suck something up and then fire it out of his mouth, dealing damage to opponents or objects around the map. Kirby's Dream Land was designed to be an easy game for beginners, but players can modify Kirby's health and maximum life count for added challenge.

Title: Lemmings
Description: Lemmings is a puzzle/strategy game for the Sega Game Gear developed by Psygnosis. Players are tasked to help rescue lemmings across the 120 levels in the game, while avoiding obstacles and hazards. The player controls a crosshair that can direct Lemmings, and each level has a different range of skills, a different amount of Lemmings, and a different percentage target in order to progress.

Description: Lifestylers is a community-based, mobile game that allows players to create their own character, or "Lifestyler," who will live life according to the player's desire.  Each Lifestyler receives a certain classification in society, such as "Casanova" or "Geek."  Lifestylers face a wide variety of situations, both exhilarating, like participating in a mystery experiment and mundane, like eating dinner. Players earn points based on how they react to these situations.  The objective of the game is for the player to earn  points towards becoming the best within their societal classification and, ultimately, to become a celebrity in their city.

Title: LocoRoco
Description: LocoRoco is a puzzle/platforming game for the Sony PSP. Players control the level's movement using the bumpers, guiding the LocoRoco to safety, avoiding enemies and obstacles. The game has 5 worlds with 8 levels in each. Score is based on amount of LocoRoco saved and time taken to complete the level, with the main goal of reaching the finish line.

Title: Mad City Mystery
Description: Players walk around the University of Wisconsin-Madison campus with a handheld GPS device, so they can try to solve the mystery of an unexpected drowning accident. They form hypotheses on what caused the person (named Larry) to drown and meet with/interact with other virtual people in the game who provide evidence, counter-evidence, and other information to help solve the mystery. The game takes anywhere between 90-120 minutes.

Title: Majestic
Description: An augmented reality game (ARG) released by Electronic Media that involved players receiving instant messages, emails, faxes, and voicemails. The game, which was marketed as an immersive science fiction thriller, was released on July 31, 2001 in five separate episodes. The purpose of the game was for players to uncover the truth behind a conspiracy. Ultimately, the game was unable to attract enough players for its paid subscription service and was canceled in 2002.
Articles: https://www.engadget.com/2013-01-26-the-game-archaeologist-eas-majestic.html (The Game Archaeologist: EA's Majestic)

Title: Mario Kart DS
Description: Mario Kart DS is a racing game developed by Nintendo featuring characters and elements from the Mario franchise. Races can have up to 8 drivers and must use powerups and attacks to speed up or slow others down. This was the first game in the series to utilize the Nintendo Wi-Fi Connection in order for players to compete over the internet. Another first for the series was using retro tracks, giving courses from previous installments of the series a modern touch up. Mario Kart DS is the third highest selling game for the Nintendo DS.
Articles: https://www.ign.com/articles/2005/11/12/mario-kart-ds (IGN: Mario Kart DS), https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/r_mariokart_ds (Eurogamer: Mario Kart DS)

Title: Mario Kart: Super Circuit
Description: Mario Kart: Super Circuit is a racing game for the Nintendo Game Boy Advance. The third entry in the series, this title  is the first to be available on a portable system. The same cast of characters from Mario Kart 64 are available in this game, as well as the same 5 game modes. Multiplayer was possible through the Game Boy Link cable. Super Circuit has 20 new courses for players to race through, as well as the 20 from Super Mario Kart (SNES).

Title: Mario Vs Donkey Kong
Description: Mario Vs Donkey Kong is a platform puzzle game for the Nintendo Gameboy Advance. Gameplay involves platforming as Mario moves through levels in order to retrieve toys that Donkey Kong stole. Stages include collecting keys to unlock the next level, guiding smaller moving toys to achieve a goal for Mario, and boss fights where Mario must defeat Donkey Kong to proceed in the game. Mario Vs Donkey Kong received favorable reviews in 2004 and a sequel was released in 2006 for the Nintendo DS.
Articles: https://www.metacritic.com/game/game-boy-advance/mario-vs-donkey-kong (Metacritic: Mario Vs Donkey Kong), https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/05/24/mario-vs-donkey-kong (IGN: Mario vs. Donkey Kong)

Title: Mario and Luigi: Superstar Saga
Description: Mario and Luigi: Superstar Saga is a role-playing game developed by AlphaDream for the Nintendo Game boy Advance. The game's narrative focuses on Mario and Luigi traveling to beat two enemies named Cackletta and Fawful, because they stole princess Peach's voice. Gameplay involves turn based combat and controlling Mario and Luigi at the same time in order to successfully defeat opponents.
Articles: https://www.ign.com/wikis/mario-luigi-superstar-saga/Walkthrough (IGN: Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga Walkthrough), https://www.metacritic.com/game/game-boy-advance/mario-luigi-superstar-saga (Metacritic: Mario and Luigi: Superstar Saga)

Title: Mario vs. Donkey Kong 2: March of the Minis
Description: Mario vs. Donkey Kong 2: March of the Minis is a Nintendo DS game and is a more puzzle oriented sequel to Mario Vs Donkey Kong from the Gameboy Advance. Players would use the DS's touch screen and stylus to influence the movement of toy "Mini-Marios" in order for them to reach a specific location and complete the level. The Mini-Marios lack self-preservation, so the player must protect them all from getting damaged and destroyed. The touchscreen would allow players to swipe, rotate, and tap the Mini-Marios in order to control their actions. The D-pad controls the camera angle.

Title: Mattel Auto Race
Description: Possibly the first mobile game and the first in the Mattel line of handheld mobile games. In this game, the player changes gears to race against red dots that represent cars. This game is often overshadowed by the more successful 'sequel' Mattel Football. The handheld was single player and required batteries.

Title: Mattel Dungeons and Dragons
Description: A handheld game console based off the RPG Dungeons and Dragons produced by Mattel. In this game, players would traverse through a maze , avoid obstacles, and slay a dragon. There are three main controls, cursor, attack, and move. The cursor would help you choose your path. Dungeons and Dragons is a bout the size of a credit card and run on two small watch batteries.

Title: Mattel Electronics Horoscope Computer
Description: The Mattel Electronics Horoscope Computer is a small handheld device that is designed to predict your horoscope and compatibility with others. Users have access to predictions for all 12 astrological signs. The other inputs are "love," "career," "travel," "money," "friends," "spirit," "family," and "creative." Users would select the astrological sign that applies to them from the circle of inputs to the left, then select a category for a prediction from the inputs to the right, and then receive a vague message in the middle of the circle. According to the instructions, the game was only accurate from June 1, 1979 to December 31, 1987.
Articles: https://www.handheldmuseum.com/Mattel/HC.htm (Handheld Museum: Computer Horoscope)

Title: Mattel Football
Description: Handheld gaming console that simulates playing football-- requires single players to move across a small rectangular (football field) screen and surpass obstacles to score.
Articles: https://www.handheldmuseum.com/Mattel/FB.htm (Catalog Entry, Handheld Museum)

Title: Mega Man V
Description: Mega Man V is an action platforming game developed by Capcom for the Nintendo Game Boy. Players control Mega Man as he traverses through levels, avoiding obstacles and taking down bosses. Once a player defeats a boss, they receive a power-up related to said boss, that helps them throughout the game. Some power-ups are more useful against certain bosses than others, so the game recommends taking them down in a specific order, if the player wants to be as effective as possible. The plot of the game reveals that Mega Man must stop a group of powerful robots called the "Stardroids" from invading Earth.

Title: Memory Race
URL: no website for the game, only for the device: https://buy.garmin.com/en-US/US/p/220#specs (Geko 201)
Description: A classic game of "matching pairs by memory" through a GPS (Garmin Geko 202) interface. The GPS interface is divided into tiles. To "flip" a tile and find matching tiles, the player must navigate in space to the position of the tile. Once a tile is flipped, the player then moves to a different location to flip another tile with the hope that both flipped tiles match one another. The game continues until the player has successfully matched all tiles, which constitutes a win.

Title: Metroid: Zero Mission
Description: Metroid: Zero Mission is an action-adventure game for the Gameboy Advance, and is a remake of the original NES Metroid game. Players control Samus Aran, a space bounty hunter, through a large open world on the planet Zebes. Power-ups are frequent throughput the world to help the player defeat Space Pirates and to access new areas of the world (with the goal to stop the Space Pirates from experimenting on Metriods). Metroid: Zero Mission features many characters and items used in the popular fighting series "Super Smash Bros."
Articles: https://www.ign.com/games/metroid-zero-mission (IGN: Metroid: Zero Mission)

Description: Handheld gaming console- uses inter-changeable cartridges, LCD screen. Game cartridges provided hardware to help system the system run, in order for it to be more compact.

Title: Missile Attack
Description: Released in 1976, this game requires the player to fire missiles at attacking adversaries, while the players aircraft stays at the bottom of the screen. This game did not sell well, due to the name and the fear of the Cold War. Mattel would eventually rename this game as Space Alert with a Battlestar Galactica theme. This console is powered by a 9V battery.

Title: Missile Defender
Description: Missile Defender is a handheld gaming console developed in 1984 by the famous watch company. the handheld is a small rectangle, with an LCD screen, two control buttons, and off and on switch, and a unique rotating input for movement. Gameplay involved the player shooting down attacking jets with a tank.
Articles: http://handheldempire.com/game.jsp?game=475 (Handheld Empire: Missile Defender)

Title: MobiMissions
Description: MobiMissions is a location-based phone experience for teens in the UK, which allows players to create or respond to missions around the city. Missions are created by players embedding photographs and text instructions onto locations. Another player can "discover" these missions by traveling to that location (the mission is found by Cell-ID), then choosing whether to follow the text instructions to complete the mission. Completing the mission requires players to document their efforts with photos and textual descriptions. The game was created for teens between the ages of 16-18 to explore, learn, and interact with people and places around the community.

Title: MobileHunters
Description: MobileHunters is a multiplayer location-based phone game. The game recognizes a player's geographic location, and sets up the playing field accordingly. The game must have 2 or more players to be played successfully. When the players join the game, they are assigned one of two roles: hunter or fugitive. The game places resources for the hunters and fugitives across the playing field, with all items in close proximity. The hunters must find weapons and go find the fugitive, while the fugitive must find protection and evidence to prove their innocence. All of these items appear as icons on the screen, and are collected when the player is in the same location as the item.
Articles: http://www.informatica.si/index.php/informatica/article/viewFile/141/133 (Mobile Location-Based Gaming as Driver for Location-Based Services (LBS) – Exemplified by Mobile Hunters)

Title: MobileMath
Developers: Monica Wijers, Vincent Jonker, Kristel Kerstens
Description: This is a location-based mobile game that uses a GPS receiver. Teams (of up to 8 players) attempt to construct geometrical shapes by physically moving to points on a map and, then, clicking each point. Since shapes cannot overlap, players can obstruct an opposing team by building a shape in the opposing team's pathway. Points are given based on the area (size) and difficulty of constructing a shape.

Description: MOGI is a Japanese hybrid reality game available from 2001-2008 via the mobile operator, KKDI's "portal" which advertised games. The game's goal was to collect location-based virtual objects and creatures around the city of Tokyo using their cell phone. To capture an object, players navigated a map with a 500 meter radius and had to come within 300 meters to catpure the object. Players could also see other nearby players on the radar of their cell phone screen and exchange virtual objects. Online players could also guide street players to find specific items for their collections. During the game's availability, there were around 1000 active players.

Title: Mole Mania
Description: Mole Mania is a puzzle game for the Nintendo Game Boy. Players control Muddy the mole as they push, pull, and throw a ball to a gate. The ball hitting the gate will allow players to advance to the next level. Players can also dig around obstacles, making holes that can help or hinder their progress. Leaving the screen and coming back resets the level, in case a mistake is made.

Title: Mother 3
Description: Mother 3 is a top-down role-playing game for the Nintendo Game Boy Advance, and the third entry in the Mother series. The game follows Lucas, a young boy with psychic powers as he recruits a party in order to stop mysterious enemies from destroying the planet. Players can control Lucas and the other party members as they explore the world, collect items, and defeat enemies. The goal of the game is to earn experience points to level the party up in order to complete the game. Mother 3 was never released outside of Japan

Title: Mr. Challenger
Description: The Mr. Challenger is an educational gaming device that has various games and a full keyboard. Three similar games are on the device, Math Marvel, Mr. Challenger, and Spelling B. The design is similar to other Texas Instrument devices. At launch, the retail price was $40 and it took 9V batteries for power.

Title: Mr. Wood Man
Description: Handheld device that was one of the first devices to hold multiple games. Mr. Wood Man had an LCD screen and came in a yellow or green colorway. Gameplay involves the player controlling 'Mr. Wood Man' (a lumberjack), going up a tree to help someone. Players must avoid falling branches and bear attacks.

Title: Musical Marvin
Description: Musical Marvin is an electronic sound based handheld game developed by Entex. It comes packed with six different games that allow for 1-4 players with speed, volume, and tone controls. The games include Musical Chairs, Mimic, Mystery Threes, Note Quote, Four Score, and Last Note. Musical Marvin can be used as a full-octave musical instrument as well. A handle is built-in and has 8 control buttons, 2 being red, 2 being blue, 2 being yellow, and 2 being green.

Title: My Little Pony: Pinkie Pie's Party
Description: My Little Pony: Pinkie Pie's Party is an adventure/puzzle game developed by Webfoot Technologies for the Nintendo DS. The plot revolves around finding hidden presents around Ponyville while playing as Pinkie Pie. Gameplay involves using the D-Pad to move around the world and tapping various items to reveal presents or to talk to other ponies.
Articles: https://www.ign.com/articles/2008/10/09/my-little-pony-pinkie-pies-party-review (IGN: My Little Pony: Pinkie Pie's Party Review)

Description: Small handheld gaming and smartphone device, featuring a color screen. Uses Nokia Series 60 Symbian OS. Has an SD card slot for games and memory cards.

Title: NBA Jam
Description: NBA Jam is a handheld port of the popular arcade game of the same name developed for a handheld by Tiger Electronics. Gameplay involved controlling two NBA players in a half court offense trying to dunk and block shots in order to outscore the other team. A classic 24 second shot clock was present like the actual NBA. The handheld has a D-pad for movement, and 4 control buttons for shooting/blocking, passing/stealing, rebounding, and a turbo button.
Articles: http://handheldempire.com/game.jsp?game=1750 (Handheld Empire: NBA Jam)

Title: Namco Museum DS
Description: Namco Museum DS is a game collection of Namco arcade games ported to the Nintendo DS. The games include: Galaxian, Pac-Man, Galaga, Xevious, Mappy, Super Xevious, The Tower of Druaga, Dig Dug 2, and Pac-Man Vs. The Pac-Man Vs game allows for multiplayer over the DS Download play, allowing for four players to compete against one another. The cartridge saves players high scores, and has menus with old promotional material and information to view, hence the museum aspect of the title.
Articles: https://www.ign.com/articles/2007/09/28/namco-museum-ds-review (IGN- Namco Museum DS Review)

Title: NavBall
Description: NavBall is a multiplayer game that used GPS phones and took place across the city of Amsterdam. Gameplay lasted 45 minutes. It featured 2 teams of 11 players each that attempt to score as many goals as possible. The “ball” and “goal” are placed on a map of Amsterdam, and the players have to get into formation to kick the “ball” at the right angle and speed to make a goal. The players have to move around the city with their GPS enabled phones in order to achieve this.

Title: Nelsonic Zelda Watch
Description: A gaming watch created by Nelsonic based on the Nintendo franchise The Legend of Zelda. The watch comes in black, pink, white or red and had four movement buttons. Gameplay is top down and involves the player controlling the main character, link through a variety of dungeons and obstacles. Similar items and enemies from the main series appear as well.

Title: Neo Geo Pocket Color
Description: The Neo Geo Pocket Color is a handheld console produced by the company SNK. At the time of release, it was marketed as a competitor to the Game Boy and Sega Game Gear. The console has a cartridge based game system and can last for 40 hours on 2 AA  batteries. The Neo Geo Pocket Color was not on the market long, due to high competition, and because SNK declared bankruptcy a few years after the game's release. A joystick, and 2 control buttons are present on the console for gameplay.
Articles: https://www.thegamer.com/best-neo-geo-pocket-color-games/ (10 Best Neo Geo Pocket Color Games), https://www.theverge.com/2012/11/23/3618196/status-symbols-neo-geo-pocket-color (Status Symbols: Neo Geo Pocket Color)

Title: Neo Turf Masters (Neo Geo Pocket Color)
Description: Neo Turf Masters is an arcade style golfing game with various levels and golfers from which to choose. Standing out from many other golfing games, in Neo Turf Masters, players would click once to swing their club and hit the ball, rather than twice. Neo Turf Masters was ported to the Neo Geo Pocket Color in 1999 from the original 1996 game. The version on the Pocket Color was less detailed and cartoonish compared to the original game.
Articles: https://www.retrogamer.net/top_10/top-ten-neo-geo-pocket-color/ (TOP TEN NEO GEO POCKET COLOR)

Title: New Super Mario Bros.
Description: New Super Mario Bros. is a 2D side scrolling platforming game for the Nintendo DS developed and published by Nintendo. It was the first 2D entry in the Super Mario franchise in almost 14 years at its release. Gameplay is similar to the rest of the 2D Super Mario platforming games, but features new powerups, levels, and enemies. Powerups include a Mega Mushroom that allows Mario to grow to gargantuan sizes. Two multiplayer modes are in the game besides the main story: a two-player VS mode and a set of minigames for up to four players. New Super Mario Bros. is the best-selling game to come out on the Nintendo DS with 30.80 million units sold according to Nintendo.

Title: Nintendo DSi XL
Description: Flip handheld gaming device, featuring dual color screens (with bottom screen serving as a touch screen). The Nintendo DSi XL has the same properties as the Nintendo DSi but is larger in size. The XL was originally released in Japan in 2009 and worldwide by 2010.

Title: Nintendo Pokémon Pikachu
Description: A mobile game console dedicated to taking care of a virtual Pikachu. Similar to other mobile pet games, such as Tamagotchi and Giga Pets. It can track steps for in game rewards.

Title: Nintendogs
Description: Nintendogs is a pet care simulation game developed by Nintendo for the Nintendo DS. Players could pick their breed of dog and raise them, using interactive elements like the touch screen and microphone  to simulate real-life activities like grooming and feeding. There are multiple versions of the game featuring different breeds of dogs on the cover, which correlates to what breeds are attainable in the game. The multiplayer element of the game involves walking your dogs and connecting with other DS consoles. Nintendogs is the second highest selling Nintendo DS game with 23.96 million units sold across the three versions of the game according to Nintendo.

Title: Noderunner
Developers: Yury Gitman, Carlos J. Gomez de Llarena
Description: In Noderunner, the cityscape of Manhattan is reterritorialized into hot and cold spots—determined by access to the Internet. The aim of the game, in which two teams are pitted against each other, is to access and document (via camera phones) as many of the wireless Internet nodes as possible while attempting to get from Bryant Park in midtown to Bowling Green in Lower Manhattan. Teams are given a Wi-Fi-enabled laptop, a digital camera, taxi fare, and 2 hours. Points are obtained by taking camera phone pictures of themselves in the exact spot at which they connected to the wireless Internet; they are also awarded points for using scanning software to find the nodes on their journey.

Title: Nokia 3310
Description: Originally released in 2000, Nokia re-released a version of the phone in 2017. The original phone had a monochrome LCD. The re-released version uses a color display and has a camera. Pre-installed games include Pairs II, Space Impact, Bantumi, and Snake II. A best seller, this phone has been immortalized due to its durability.

Title: Oil Gang
Description: Handheld game that includes an alarm and date functions. The console requires 2 AG13 batteries and had four movement buttons and two buttons for settings. The game involved stopping an open oil pipe from spilling into the ocean.
Articles: https://artsandculture.google.com/asset/handheld-video-game-oil-gang-epoch-co-ltd/sAHQjqWG9IgarQ?hl=en (The Strong National Museum of Play: Oil Gang)

Title: One Piece
Description: One Piece is a 2-D platforming game for the Nintendo Game Boy Advance, based of the popular anime/manga of the same name. Players control Straw Hat Luffy as he traverses through levels based on story arcs from the series, beating up enemy marines and pirates. Characters such as Zoro and Sanji can be summoned throughout the game after they are unlocked, and assist Luffy in defeating bosses and enemies. This is the only One Piece game to be exclusively released in the United States.

Title: Operation Urban Terrain
Description: Operation Urban Terrain was a piece of performance art in the form of a mobile "game" that happened in 2004. Lead by Anne Marie Schleiner, two women formed the "ground unit" and were connected via a mobile internet connection to a team of players in a form of mixed reality gaming. This game was intended to protest the use of military simulation games to train military during the Republican National Convention during that time and was in general an anti-war protest.
Articles: https://www.vdb.org/titles/out-operation-urban-terrain (Video Data Bank Catalog)

Title: PAC-LAN
Description: A location-based version of Pac-Man, in which Pac-Man players and Ghosts are equipped with Nokia phones that have an RFID tag embedded in the shell of the phone. Both Pac-Man and Ghost Players move around a physical space to collect pills (discs with RFID tags). However, ghosts can also collect pills which give them points and allow them to know the last position of the Pac-Man players. If the Pac-Man player collects a "power pill," then the Pac-Man player can kill ghosts, which forces them to return to the central location of the maze.  The game took place at Alexandra Park of the Lancaster University campus

Title: Pac-Man (Neo Geo Pocket Color)
Description: Pac-Man for the Neo Geo Pocket Color is a mobile version of the classic arcade game. Players must traverse a maze as Pac-Mac, eating dots and avoiding ghosts. The goal is to eat all the dots on the board to progress to the next level.
Articles: https://hardcoregamer.com/features/pocket-power/pocket-power-pac-man/46429/ (Pocket Power: Pac-Man)

Title: PacManhattan
Description: PacManhattan consisted of playing the game Pac-Man within the actual streets of Manhattan. A person dressed as Pac-Man (wearing yellow) tried to avoid being “eaten” by ghost (players dressed in primary colors). At the same time, the Pac-Man player attempted to "eat" virtual dots on the streets to score points. In a remote location, players in a control room updated the street player’s physical position on a digital map of the city. The only way for the street players to know which dots have already been eaten is by talking to his or her controller.

Description: Parallel Kingdom uses GPS and a mobile app (on iOS and Android platforms) to allow users to create virtual domains of physical places. The object of the game is to dominate or take ownership of physical spaces. To do so, players can play individually or in teams. Gameplay involves locating resources and battling other players to achieve ownership of a place.

Title: Pichu Bros. mini
Description: Pichu Bros. mini is a party game for the Pokémon Mini, based on the anime Pichu Bros. The game is a compellation of six mini-games, similar to the Pokémon Party mini game. The Cubone and Battlefield games can be played with others, over the consoles infrared connectivity. A Pokémon themed clock application is also available through he games menus.

Title: Pinball
Description: Small handheld device/game, allowing navigational control and two unique input controls (punch, kick/accelerate, break). The handheld took two AA batteries, and were marketed as being cheaper than the Nintendo Game Boy. Players can control both flippers like on a physical pinball machine.

Title: Pinball
Description: Pinball is a handheld game developed by Gakken. The console is small and rectangular, with red, white, and blue on its face. The screen is LCD with the outline of a pinball machine, including two bumper buttons. This version of pinball also included a time and alarm function.

Title: Ping Pong Plus
Description: A game of ping-pong featuring a reactive table that incorporates sound and projection technology. The way the ball hits the table can change how the projections visualize.
Articles: https://tangible.media.mit.edu/project/pingpongplus/ (PingPongPlus), https://www.academia.edu/34299489/PingPongPlus (Hiroshi Ishii Article)

Title: Pocket Bomberman
Description: Pocket Bomberman is a side-scrolling platformer for the Nintendo Game Boy Color. Gameplay involves players controlling Bomberman as he traverses through levels, dropping bombs to clear obstacles and destroy enemies. The game has 25 different levels and, in order to progress, the player must eliminate every enemy on said level. Pocket Bomberman was a launch title for the Game Boy Color, and was the first in the series to not have a top-down perspective.

Title: Pokemon Ranger: Shadows of Almia
Description: Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia is an action/role-playing game for the Nintendo DS and the first sequel to Pokémon Ranger. Core gameplay differs from traditional Pokémon games, allowing players to use the "capture styler" to catch Pokémon, rather than the standard Pokeballs. Players use the touch-screen and the stylus to capture Pokémon, capturing different Pokémon allows the styler to be upgraded with different buffs. Shadows of Almia features a new story, more Pokémon (notably from the 4th generation of main-series games), and a capturing gameplay change, making players boost friendship level thorough carefully drawing circles with the stylus.
Articles: https://www.ign.com/articles/2008/11/11/pokemon-ranger-shadows-of-almia-review (IGN: Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia Review)

Title: Pokémon Breeder mini
Description: Pokémon Breeder mini is a simulation game for the Pokémon Mini handheld. Players have the ability to choose and care for a Treeko, Torchic, or Mudkip, the three starters from the third generation of Pokémon games. Feeding, playing with, and training are vital parts of the gameplay, with the main goal of maxing out the four skills that one of the selected Pokémon can have. Love, strength, energy, and intellect stats must me maximized in order for the player to complete or beat the game.

Title: Pokémon Dash
Description: Pokémon Dash is a top-down racing game for the Nintendo DS and the first Pokémon game released for the console. Players use the console's stylus and touchscreen to control Pikachu as he races through a map, passing checkpoints and other Pokémon. Courses have various terrain that can help or hinder a player and power-ups that can help them speed up or power through rough areas. Pokémon Dash has a training mode and  Grand Prix mode, which includes 5 cups with 5 races in each. Up to 6 players can compete against one another in races through the DS Download Play. Dash features compatibility with the Game Boy Advance games Pokémon Ruby, Sapphire, Fire Red, Leaf Green, or Emerald. If the player inserts any of those cartridges in Slot 2, and has completed GP mode, they can play courses shaped like the Pokémon in their team. The time to complete the courses depends on factors like type and level.

Title: Pokémon Diamond and Pearl
Description: Pokémon Diamond and Pearl are part of the 4th generation of Pokémon games developed by Game Freak. Diamond and Pearl are almost identical story wise. Gameplay is similar to other entries of the series, where players collect, train, and battle Pokémon in order to beat the game. Diamond and Pearl were the first games in the series to feature online multiplayer for trading and battling. This generation of games introduced 107 new Pokémon, and both games were required to collect them all. Remakes for both games were released in November of 2021 for the Nintendo Switch.
Articles: https://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/2007/04/pokemon_diamond_and_pearl_ds (Pokémon Diamond & Pearl Review)

Title: Pokémon Party mini
Description: Pokémon Party mini is a multiplayer handheld game for the Pokémon Mini device. The game allows players to choose from 7 different mini games, as well as utilize a clock feature. The two game modes that are multiplayer are Sneasel's Fake Out and Battlefield, the rest are singe player. Europe and North America had this game included with the purchase of the Pokémon Mini console, which had infrared capabilities for multiplayer games.

Title: Pokémon Pikachu 2 GS
Description: Small pedometer wearable that players could strap to their belt. For each kilometer walked, the player would receive "1 watt" which was in-game currency that would allow them to gamble and/or purchase gifts for Pikachu, the character of the game. Additionally, the  The purpose of the game is to make Pikachu happy and to increase the friendship level with Pikachu. The game featured an alarm and color-screen.
Articles: https://www.engadget.com/products/nintendo/pokemon/pikachu/2-gs/ (Engadget: Nintendo Pokémon Pikachu 2 GS)

Title: Pokémon Pinball mini
Description: Pokémon Pinball mini is a pinball game for the Pokémon Mini handheld. Players have the option to play 90 different pinball levels, including 70 in a quest mode and 10 for a Time Attack and Score Attack mode. Quest mode is the main style of the game, players complete one level to unlock the next, players fill holes in the board and aim to reach high scores. Time Attack is strictly filling holes, and Score Attack is strictly for scoring points. The Pokémon Diglett is used at the paddle and a Pokeball is used as the main ball.

Title: Pokémon Pinball: Ruby & Sapphire
Description: Pokémon Pinball: Ruby & Sapphire is a pinball game for the Nintendo Game Boy Advance featuring Pokémon from the 1st-3rd generation. It is the sequel to the Game Boy's Pokémon Pinball game from 1999. Gameplay is that of a normal pinball game, but allows for players to capture, collect, and defeat Pokémon with their skill. Various items and characters from the series appear on the games boards to help or hinder the players progress. There are 205 Pokémon to collect in the game.

Title: Pokémon Platinum
Description: Pokémon Platinum is the third entry of the 4th generation of Pokémon games developed by Game Freak. Platinum acts as an enhanced edition of Pokémon Diamond and Pearl, offering players speedier gameplay and a new story. New areas and forms of Pokémon are introduced as well, making Platinum one of the best esteemed games in the franchise. Like many other special editions of Pokémon games (Emerald and Silver), Platinum was designed to be the ultimate version of the generation.

Title: Pokémon Puzzle Collection
Description: Pokémon Puzzle Collection is a puzzle game for the Pokémon Mini handheld. Gameplay features four original puzzle games including: Motion, Shadow, Rescue Mission, and Power On. All puzzle games revolve around shifting blocks or pieces in order to form a shape, escape an entrapment, or connect circuits together, using sliding motions to complete them. After completing 30 puzzles the Power Up mode is unlocked. Each mode has 20 puzzles, divided into five levels with four puzzles each.

Title: Pokémon Puzzle Collection vol. 2
Description: Pokémon Puzzle Collection vol. 2  is a puzzle game for the Pokémon Mini handheld, only released in Japan. The game has 4 modes, 2 new ones and 2 returning from the previous game. Motion Puzzles and Shadow Puzzles return, Pick Up Puzzles and Stitch Puzzles are introduced. Each puzzle has 20 different stages, all modes are unlocked from the start, and completing a stage unlocks the next as well as catches a Pokémon players can view from the Mini Dex menu.

Title: Pokémon Race mini
Description: Pokémon Race mini is a racing game for the Pokémon Mini handheld. Players control Pikachu as they race other Pokémon while avoiding obstacles like grass and water. Pokémon that race against Pikachu have different buffs that assist them, for example, Chikorita is not slowed by grass. The game has 16 levels, and 5 modes including: Pokémon Grand Prix, Challenge, Time Attack, and Ditto Battle, and Rankings.

Title: Pokémon Ranger
Description: Pokémon Ranger is an action/role-playing game for the Nintendo DS. Core gameplay differs from traditional Pokémon games, allowing players to use the "capture styler" to catch Pokémon, rather than the standard Pokeballs. Players use the touch-screen and the stylus to capture Pokémon, capturing different Pokémon allows the styler to be upgraded with different buffs. The plot involves the player controlling Lunick or Solana in their quest to capture Pokémon and stop the evil Go-Rock squad. Pokémon Ranger would receive two sequels following its success.
Articles: https://www.ign.com/articles/2006/11/03/pokemon-ranger-review (IGN: Pokémon Ranger Review)

Title: Pokémon Red and Blue
Description: Pokémon Red, Blue, Green, Yellow are the first generation of Pokémon games developed by Nintendo and Game Freak. Both games are for the Nintendo Game Boy and were rereleased on the Nintendo 3DS E-Shop. Pokémon is an RPG where player collect, train, and evolve creatures called Pokémon in order to win battles, beat villainous organizations, or catch every Pokémon. The success of both early games launched Pokémon into being the most valuable franchise in media.  Differences between the games included Pokémon you could catch or win as a prize. Players can interact via a Game Boy link cable.

Title: Pokémon Tetris
Description: Pokémon Tetris is a puzzle game for the Pokémon Mini handheld. Gameplay requires players to rotate falling shapes in order to create lines, once a line is complete it will disappear and a Pokémon on the left of the screen will be caught and added to the Pokedex. The various game modes include Standard (with three difficulties: Rookie, Normal, and Hyper,) 20 Lines (a time test to see if the player can fill 20 lines), Pyramid (a challenge to see if the player can complete 1-4 lines), Pokedex (a menu to view captured Pokémon), and VS. Multiplayer is possible through the VS mode if two players have a game cartridge. The VS mode is the same as Standard, but if a player completes a line, the other player receives an extra one.

Title: Pokémon Trozei!
Description: Pokémon Trozei! is a puzzle game for the Nintendo DS. Players match blocks shaped like Pokémon in order to clear ways for new blocks, reaching scores, completing levels, and collecting Pokémon by matching them. Game modes include, Adventure (a story mode), Endless (a challenge mode that lasts 145 levels), Forever (a harder challenge mode that never ends), and Pokedex (a menu where players can view Pokémon they have captured/matched.) Multiplayer is accessible through the DS's infrared capabilities, allowing players to challenge each other and earn higher scores.

Title: Pokémon Zany Cards
Description: Pokémon Zany Cards is a handheld virtual card game for the Pokémon Mini handheld. There are 4 game modes, 3 of which allow for multiplayer (Wild Match, Special Seven and Card Duel.) The only single player game mode is Four Kings. All game modes are unique to Pokémon Zany Cards, and feature new mechanics and Pokémon from the main series of games.

Title: Pooyan
Description: Pooyan is a handheld LCD game developed by Gakken, based of the arcade game/franchise. Gameplay involved players controlling a pig on a lift while shooting down attacking wolves that are floating on balloons. Controls include a shoot button, up/down buttons, and score is kept as the player shoots more wolves. The LCD screen is surrounded by colorful art of the characters in the game.

Title: R-Zone
Description: The R-Zone is a handheld system that tried to capitalize on the craze of virtual reality. Users view games on a half-mirrored eyepiece attached to a headset worn via a headband. This system was Tiger's first to allow for multiple games to be played with one system; each interchangeable game cartridge included its own red-colored LCD screen. Many licensed games exist for it, including games based off Batman Forever and The Lost World: Jurassic Park.

Title: RAZR
Description: Thin flip phone with mini USB port, digital camera, a predecessor of the StarTAC. The RAZR had a clamshell design with an internal and external glass screen. Headphone are able to be attached and a mini-USB port is present for charging. It is credited as the best selling clamshell phone. An updated touchscreen model that folds was released in 2020.

Title: REXplorer

Description: REXplorer is a mobile, pervasive spell-casting game designed for tourists of Regensburg, Germany. The game creates player encounters with spirits (historical figures) that are associated with significant buildings in an urban setting. A novel mobile interaction mechanism of “casting a spell” (making a gesture by waving a mobile phone through the air) allows the player to awaken and communicate with a spirit to continue playing the game. The game is designed to inform visitors about history in a fun manner.

Title: Rabbit Hop
Description:
Game/console with three screens that folds-in and offers four different games. Has navigational control, music on/off controls. The game required players to control a rabbit while dodging items thrown at them by kids and a bear.

The game was also released in Germany under the name Zeit & Spass

Players then try to shoot ghosts by moving in their direction. The faster a player moves, the more powerful the shot. The energy of a shot “annoys” ghosts, and a player can expect more ghosts after shooting one. In RayGun, each player has only limited access to the virtual game world, and the level of immersion in the game depends on the player’s imagination.

Title: RealReplay
Description: RealReplay is a location-based game where players create their own race track using their device's GPS. Other players can then race along the player's created racetrack. The game supports races on bikes, skates, sailing boats, or on foot.

Title: Rhythm Heaven
Description: Rhythm Heaven is a music/rhythm game for the Nintendo DS. This game required players to hold their DS sideways and use the touchscreen. A left-handed mode was also available. A collection of rhythm/mini games compose the entire game. Controls required players to use the DS stylus for tapping, holding, sliding and flicking, or the left and right buttons for playing Rockers 2 (a game within the game). Rhythm Heaven was the first game in the series to be released outside of Japan.
Articles: https://www.wired.com/2009/04/review-rhythm-h/ (Review: Rhythm Heaven Is Portable Musical Brilliance)

Title: Rider Spoke
Description: Rider Spoke (2007) is a location-based game developed by Blast Theory. Cyclists mount a Nokia N800 to the handlebars of their bicycles before heading out into the city. Using WiFi fingerprinting to determine location, the device guides users to various hiding places throughout the area. At each hiding place, the user is asked to answer a question or share a story via a voice recording on their device. Users can also find locations where other cyclists have left responses and listen to those as well.

Title: Savannah
Developers: K. Facer, R. Joiner, D. Stanton, J. Reid, R. Hull, D. Kirk
Description: Savannah is a game that was designed as a study to offer insights as to how mobile gaming can support learning. It was target towards kids between the ages of 11 and 12. The children were given GPSs that were linked to PDAs. Through the PDAs they could see, hear, and “smell” their surroundings in the virtual Savannah. There were two domains for the game. The first was an outdoor area that measured 100m x 50m. In this area, the kids would interact with a virtual Savannah and try to survive as lions in the wild. The children were exposed to real risks of being a lion in the Savannah and tried to survive. The other domain was an indoor space called the “Den”.  This space was a space where children would reflect on how well they survived and used their resources. While in the Savannah, the children would see still images of their environment that simulated scents or images the lions would see. They had an energy bar that would let them know if they were too hot or too hungry. They were also able to send information back to the Den to look back at later.

Title: The Journey II

Description: The Journey II is an attempt to introduce more narrative into an adventure game. Players solve mysteries by progressing through the story and going to actual physical locations as indicated by the story. Instead of changing the gameplay on the basis of the player’s location, the game builds a virtual game environment as soon as it realizes that the player has moved. For example, at the start of the game the player’s real home can be the office, and when asked to go to another location, such as a park, the player has to move in the real world. As soon as the game detects a change in Cell ID, it prompts the player that he or she has reached the new location (the park), which in reality could be any location in the physical world. This in turn creates a virtual world as the story unfolds and the player moves back and forth through the game world until the mystery is solved.

Title: The Songs of North
Description: The Songs of North was a pervasive mobile game prototype developed by researchers at the University of Tempere in Finland. Players acted as a shaman with the ability to interact with the Spirit World through a drum. Events happened in the game based on the players location in the physical world. Players used the number keys on their mobile phone to activate the drum and participate in game events. The game encouraged collaboration with other players. The main functionality and tie to the real world was the use of sound as an indicator that an event was nearby. Players were expected to wear headphones or have the volume up on their phone to hear auditory cues. The developers intended for these cues to bring the game world and the real world closer together. There was no clear end goal to the game; only an indeterminant number of puzzles for the player to solve.

Title: Tracking Agama
Description: Tracking Agama is played with a cell phone, using downtown Los Angeles as the game board. Players’ ultimate goal is to find the fictitious character Agama by exploring clues hidden in the city landscape. The online blog is the starting point of the game, where players can learn about Agama’s story and get the first tip on where to start the game in the city. From there, players collect clues  and codes physically embedded in city landmarks. The clues and codes are either sent via SMS or used as a passcode to unlock Agama's voicemail system. Doing so gives the player information and directions to the next location.

Title: TurboExpress
Description: The TurboExpress released in late 1990 in Japan and in the United States, it was released as the TurboExpress Handheld Entertainment System. It is a portable version of the TurboGrafx-16 home console that came two to three years earlier. The TurboExpress used interchangeable cartridges for games (the same cartridges used for the home console). It was a technologically advanced game of the time, allowing for dynamic graphics and the ability to display a large amount of sprites (i.e., two-dimensional images or animations overlaid into a scene) at a time. The game allowed two-player gameplay using a Turbolink cable.

Description: Multiplayer, hybrid reality game in which remote online players use a virtual map to support a physical world player in navigating a city. The purpose of the game is for both the physical world and online player to find a character, Uncle Roy, in under sixty minutes. The game does not make use of location services. Rather, online players guess at the location of the players in the city by seeing what part of a city map that the physical world player is looking at on their PDA. Upon finding Uncle Roy, the physical world player is invited to exchange contact information with the online player, making a commitment to be there for the online player for one year.

Title: ZoneMaster
Description: Developed in Denmark in 2001, ZoneMaster was one of the first "area control" based games. Players would collect hordes of zombies to fight one another, in GPS positioned zones around Denmark.
